predecessors.name: Mughal Empire
predecessors.text: the Mughal province of Awadh, of which Saadat Khan was appointed governor on 9 September 1722

successors.name: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)
successors.text: the Kingdom of Awadh annexed by the East India Company on 11 February 1856 (the infobox of the Wajid Ali Shah page says 7 February)

ledger.x: 1722: Saadat Khan founds the Nawabi of Awadh.
1737: Balwant Singh of Benares takes Varanasi, Chunar and the Jaunpur jagirs as Awadh's zamindar.
16 August 1765: the Treaty of Allahabad takes the Allahabad district from Awadh.
ledger.cpn: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)

ledger.x: 1774: Awadh and the Company's brigade invade Rohilkhand.
7 October 1774: the treaty of Lal Dang ends the Rohilla War.
1775: Benares and its country pass to the East India Company.
ledger.cpn: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)

ledger.x: 1775 (bridged): Kora and the Doab districts return to Awadh.
1775: Asaf-ud-Daula moves the capital from Faizabad to Lucknow.
1801: the Nawab cedes half of Awadh to the Company.
ledger.cpn: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)

ledger.x: 1818: Awadh declares itself independent of the Mughals.

ledger.cpn: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)

ledger.x: February 1856: the Kingdom of Awadh ends.

wars.name: Third Battle of Panipat
wars.outcome: The Nawab of Awadh joined Ahmad Shah Durrani; Shuja-ud-Daula 'commanded a sizeable army of Mughal Sepoy, who cut off the supplies of the Marathas'.

wars.name: Battle of Buxar and the Treaty of Allahabad
wars.outcome: 22-23 October 1764: the Company defeats Shah Alam II, Mir Qasim and Shuja-ud-Daula; 'Shuja-ud-Daula fled west ... eventually surrendered'.

wars.name: Rohilla War
wars.outcome: Miranpur Katra, 23 April 1774: Hafiz Rahmat Khan killed; Rohilkhand falls to Awadh; the treaty of Lal Dang (7 October 1774) leaves Faizullah Khan the princely state of Rampur.

wars.name: Cession of 1801
wars.outcome: Not a war: a treaty cession of the Gorakhpur and Rohilkhand divisions and six Doab districts for protection against a threatened invasion by Zaman Shah Durrani.

certainty.note: Mughal province and district limits; the Himalayan Tarai frontier, the Doab frontier and the Benares country were never surveyed.
The frontier with the Company follows the districts named in the 1801 cession; the Nepal Tarai frontier stays soft.
